scope: Bounded one-vCPU stability closure combines the earlier seven-workload stress-v1 success with source56 IO probe 3: eight block flush/reopen rounds, 4,096 isolated Ethernet request/reply frames and host-observed ACPI S5.
limitations: The successful bounded run uses a 32 MiB synthetic virtio block file and an isolated in-process Ethernet peer; it does not qualify physical media, host networking, TCP/IP or an external endpoint.

Eight guest fsync rounds, eight host flush callbacks and the runner's post-poweroff reopened-byte gate qualify this fixture contract; they do not establish crash recovery, power-loss durability, reboot recovery or a host filesystem guarantee.

The network gate covers 4,096 strictly reconciled 1,024-byte request/reply frames over 18.4086489 guest seconds with one outstanding frame. It does not cover packet loss, retry, high queue depth, multi-queue, multi-vCPU or long soak.

P02-25 is satisfied by two separate bounded one-vCPU guest runs: stress-v1 covers allocation/process/filesystem/compression/clock work and this run covers block/network I/O. The workloads were not simultaneous in one guest invocation.

Source56 includes the reduced PSHUFLW correction and other intervening CPU fixes. This success validates the combined frozen source and exact guest inputs; it does not isolate EVENT_IDX or PSHUFLW as the sole cause of either earlier failure.
The experimental host and elapsed times are engineering observations, not P14 performance qualification. JIT hot sites are capped live entries rather than cumulative reason totals.
